## I2
One-Sentence Story: Memory writing should depend on future recoverability of an observation.
Theme: Efficiency and Systems
Direction Axis: memory-access-and-use
Target Failure: memory-use-and-attribution-gap
Direction Evidence: Robot motion can make discarded observations recoverable or permanently unavailable.
Form: new mechanism
Summary: Allocate writes using predicted revisit cost.
Minimal Falsification Experiment: Train on 2,000 simulated delivery episodes using 1 A100-day. Compare revisit-cost writing with validation-best surprise, recency and uniform writing. Match histories, backbone, eight slots and total action budget. Test 200 paired episodes each with reversible and one-way routes. Measure successful deliveries/200. Expect ≥10-point gain specifically on one-way routes. Kill claim if interaction <5 points; kill writer if overall gain ≤0. Shuffle route costs as attribution control.
Why It May Be Novel: Test recoverability as the variable governing memory allocation.
story: Memory writing should depend on future recoverability of an observation.
